summary: The blueprint broadly covers human pancreas but needs targeted refinements to endothelial gating, stromal/mural separation, and ambiguous progenitor/beta-maturation axes.

issues.description: The lymphatic endothelial axis is gated by a vascular/blood endothelial module that includes VWF, KDR, EMCN, and PLVAP, which may suppress true lymphatic endothelial cells rather than simply restricting the axis to endothelial cells.
issues.suggested_fix: Split a general endothelial_core module from blood/vascular endothelial markers, then gate vascular and lymphatic refinement axes on endothelial_core.

issues.description: Mural cells are contrasted against fibroblast matrix, while pericyte/smooth-muscle and stellate/myofibroblast modules share several contractile markers, blurring pericytes, smooth muscle, and activated pancreatic stellate cells.
issues.suggested_fix: Separate pericyte and smooth-muscle/contractile emphasis where possible and make mural identity a plain or stromal-gated refinement rather than a direct contrast against fibroblast matrix.

issues.description: The progenitor-like module mixes ductal/progenitor markers with endocrine-lineage markers. With no age specified, it is ambiguous: it only partially covers developmental pancreas if all ages are intended, but in adult healthy pancreas it may behave like ductal/endocrine mixing or stress.
issues.suggested_fix: Retune and name this as a clear rare developmental or immature endocrine program if all ages are meant to be covered; otherwise narrow or de-emphasize it for adult healthy pancreas use.

issues.description: The beta_mature_secretory module is mostly a subset of beta_cell, so the beta_maturation axis may duplicate beta identity instead of resolving maturity.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the positive module more specifically mature beta and use a negative module representing immature or dedifferentiated beta/endocrine state rather than the broad mixed progenitor-like module.

issues.description: The pan-epithelial module includes ductal-skewed markers such as KRT19, MUC1, and CLDN4, so it may not be a neutral epithelial gate across acinar, ductal, and endocrine compartments.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a cleaner epithelial/core gate with broadly expressed epithelial junction or cytokeratin genes, or reduce reliance on this module as the common gate for all epithelial refinements.

out_of_scope: The generic stress-state axes are plausible but dataset-dependent; keeping all of them is not inherently wrong for a broad pancreas embedding.
